lines.trans: Oh, Nikita, what are you doing here?
I stained my shirt, so I stopped in to wash it.
And why did you come down here, Lyova?
I also came to wash my uniform.
Maybe you can come back later, after me?
No, I cannot walk around the dining room with a stain.
And you can, the guests do not see you.
I am not allowed to either under sanitary rules.
Let's each prepare half of the fish.
It is a shame to waste a whole fish on your humiliation.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты теперь в официантку будешь превращаться!
examples.trans: Now you will start turning into a waitress!

examples.text: Ну и кто же теперь из нас голубок?
examples.trans: Well, and which one of us is the lovebird now?

examples.text: Хорошо, теперь твой ход, пробуй.
examples.trans: Alright, now it is your move, taste it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сегодня самый лучший день в моей жизни.
examples.trans: Today is the very best day of my life.

examples.text: А вы думали, что от меня избавились?
examples.trans: And did you think that you had gotten rid of me?

examples.text: Вы от меня не избавились!
examples.trans: You did not get rid of me!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'dove (female), pigeon' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Счастливо вам оставаться, молодые голубки!
examples.trans: Have a nice time staying here, young lovebirds!

examples.text: Ну и кто же теперь из нас голубок?
examples.trans: Well, and which one of us is the lovebird now?

examples.text: Белая голубка.
examples.trans: White dove.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'огласный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('agree').

examples.text: Я согласен.
examples.trans: I agree.

examples.text: Я согласен на этот спор!
examples.trans: I agree to this bet!

examples.text: Ладно, я согласна на этот план.
examples.trans: Alright, I agree to this plan.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Скрипач и каратист, я бы сходил на такое кино!
examples.trans: A violinist and karate fighter, I would go see that movie!

examples.text: У меня всего один месяц остался!
examples.trans: I only have one month left!

examples.text: Нет, я не могу с пятном по залу ходить.
examples.trans: No, I cannot walk around the dining room with a stain.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.text: Одного миллиграмма её яда хватит, чтобы убить.
examples.trans: One milligram of its poison is enough to kill.

examples.text: Согласен, мне и одной половины хватит.
examples.trans: Agreed, one half will be plenty for me.

examples.text: Денег не хватило.
examples.trans: There wasn't enough money.
